diagnosis: The BRAF p.V600E–RAS score (BRS) with the list of RAS-like and BRAF p.V600E–like molecular alterations
legend: A Thyroid samples (N = 391) were ranked by BRS, with BRAF p.V600E–like and RAS-like samples having negative (−1 to 0) and positive (0 to 1) scores, respectively. The BRS is strongly associated with driver mutation status (B), thyroid differentiation score (C), single data-type clusters (D), and histology and follicular fraction (E). The RAS-like samples (normalized score > 0, in red on the top bar) consistently emerged as a distinct subgroup characterized by a higher thyroid differentiation score.

diagnosis: Role of thyroid differentiation in papillary thyroid carcinomas
legend: Thyroid differentiation score (TDS) across the cohort, with tumours sorted by driver mutation and TDS. Below the TDS are the BRAF p.V600E–RAS score (BRS), ERK signature, histological type, MACIS score (distant metastasis, patient age, completeness of resection, local invasion, and tumour size), risk of recurrence, driver mutations, and gene expression data for nine thyroid genes used to derive the TDS (TG, TPO, SLC26A4 [encoding pendrin], SLC5A5 [encoding the sodium/iodide symporter], SLC5A8 [apical iodide transporter], DIO1, DIO2, DUOX1, and DUOX2), four selected mRNAs correlated to the TDS, and three selected microRNAs correlated to the TDS. Featured mRNA (except for 16 thyroid genes) and microRNA genes were selected on the basis of the Spearman correlation to the TDS in the BRAF p.V600E cohort (single asterisk) and the full cohort (double asterisk).

diagnosis: Risk of structural disease recurrence in patients without structurally identifiable disease after initial therapy
legend: The risks of structural disease recurrence associated with selected clinicopathological features are shown as a continuum of risk with percentages (ranges, approximate values) presented to reflect our best estimates based on the published literature reviewed in the text. On the left, the 3-tiered risk system proposed as the Modified Initial Risk-Stratification System is also presented to demonstrate how the continuum of risk estimates informed our modifications of the 2009 American Thyroid Association (ATA) Initial Risk System (see Recommendation 48). Although analysis of BRAF and/or TERT status (asterisks) is not routinely recommended for initial risk stratification, we have included these findings to assist clinicians in proper risk stratification in cases where this information is available. ETE, extrathyroidal extension; FTC, follicular thyroid carcinoma; FV, follicular variant; LN, lymph node; PTMC, papillary thyroid microcarcinoma; PTC, papillary thyroid carcinoma.
